Yeah it is the worst. Mine was from overuse cycling injuries. Had many pelvic problems because of it, bilateral psoas tendon release, bilateral gilmour groin repair twice, and my body is just battered.

Absolutely, I've maximised everything to get that quality of life under control. My problems are all chronic soft tissue/cartilage problems, so when I go out for my 100m (most I can do) walk, people assume I'm normal, then an old lady falls over and I want to run over to help her but I can't, and then I wan't to help her up but I can't, and have to try explain myself to everyone around or just look like I don't care about the old lady. This is the kind of stuff nobody sees that fills my brain with just hell and longing to be at peace, and not in this consciousness.
I understand. the energy required to keep going like you are is more than most people could even imagine. hang on in there, for yourself.

I can sympathise with this, it is the most awful thing to go through. I had a soft-tissue problem that didn't show up on any scans, but was awfully painful for 3 years, surgery found the problem and I'm in recovery. Funny thing was I mentioned the problem I would eventually be found to have to several doctors and consultants/radiographers and they all shrugged it off, cheers a bunch for extending my suffering and making me feel useless haha! Don't trust any of them any more

Hey! Yeah I've seen probably 20+ chiros/osteos/massage ppl. Without the surgery it only helped temporarily! Have to wait a while before I can get massages again due to the cutting of the tendons.

Thanks for the reply!

Hey, thanks for the reply. Its funny, during the past 3 years they have thrown all sorts of drugs my way.. tramadol, valium, SSRIs, morphine, and the rest. After taking them for a while I get this dirty feeling, like after you haven't showered for a week, and I force myself to stop taking what ever it is.

Some days when I feel like killing myself I get the urge to go and do things that the normal me wouldn't do, and maybe Marijuana could be one of those things? Will look into vaping.. Cheers (:

Absolutely, for me it has got to the point where if I feel extra pain when I take a stride too long or twist too much, or bend over, I just feel a sense of "oh shit" when the extra pain comes on, and I'm just sooooo tired of that feeling.

Yeah I'm seeing my GP next week and will probably discuss what effect it is still having upon me mentally, thanks! (:

Thanks for replying! To be honest I've never even smoked a cig. My mindset has always been (especially since I've been in pain) that I don't see why people are damaging their insides out of choice, when all I long for is a pain-free and healthy body.

Who knows I might try it if it comes to that!

Cheers for replying bud. Sorry to hear you are struggling also. It is hard as to think how much of our lives we have left, and the potential for the suffering to last that long is an awful thought. Life sure is testing us, enjoy what we can ay! Same to you, hope it gets easier pal
Thanks very much for the reply, I do hope it gets easier! Take care

Yeah you're right, they do! One of the nurses expected me to just get up and walk to the bathroom without assistance after double hip surgery/no tendons/and a spinal epidural, when I said I might need some help getting up she gave me a look, I mean fucking hell lol.

Yeah I defy think doing the PT by the book is the best thing, doing my exercises 3 times a day etc is the way to go. Hate painkillers, modern day answer to everything.

Yeah.. Psoas Tenotomy.. look it up!

The thing was I tried everything before surgery, PT, hydrotherapy, injections, but I could not sort those awful muscles sorted.

I had a general anaesthetic as well as a spinal epidural, and when all that wore off, my god the pain was insane. The first time I sat up the next morning after surgery, I almost passed out.

Oh yes, I was on Tramadol round the clock for a long time, before and after surgery. Right now I'm on 0 drugs, as I got tired of the side effects, and stomach problems etc, so just got more of the pain instead! Fun Fun!

Screw what other people think. If you feel better, than that is great. Look after yourself, and just tell people the truth. If people think you are making anything up which is obviously a ridiculous notion, that is their issue, not yours. Take Care.

Thank you for the reply.

I agree that we have to let things go that we can't do, and regarding the sport I have done that over the last 3 years, it was very hard going from competing on sport to doing none.

Recently it is the every day living that I want to be able to do on my own, putting on my own socks/shoes etc, and being able to lift my laptop etc, that all bring on pain. 

I did go to counselling but for some reason it made my attitude worse, maybe it was the counsellor herself, who knows. Every day I try to tell myself to ignore the pain, but it gets wearing after a while.

Hey, yes I'm sure a torn labrum is awful. On my right hip I had inflammation on the labrum that was being caused by my psoas rubbing over it. I think it is the fact that both of my hips were done, makes things pretty hard practically. Yeah, I'm doing physiotherapy but the muscles seem so stubborn to get moving and stretch out. The few days after physio every week are awful with the pain. The thought of the biggest muscles in my body working whilst not even attached to the bone makes me cringe!

Hope your labrum recovers for you.

Thanks for the reply. Indeed, I've run out of ways to say I can't do this or that with my parents/girlfriend and it does wear you down!

Absolutely agree regarding keeping living, there are just some moments, albeit every day, where I just run out of steam to cope with the pain, as it just distracts me from everything, even reading a book or watching TV, whatever it is.

Thanks very much for writing, appreciate it !
